# Draft:Timeline of intelligence in the United States

1770–1780
* Culper Spy Ring infiltrates the British Army
* Nathan Hale appointed the first Spymaster of the United States
* Nathan Hale dies
1850–1860
* The Pinkertons infiltrate labor unions and participate in strike busting
1860–1870
* Underground Railroad operates from the slaveholding states in the south through to Canada
* Harriet Tubman uses a network of slaves as an intelligence network to feed information to the Union Army
1890–1900
* (1898) United States Secret Service infiltrates the Spanish government and dismantles the Montreal Spy Ring
1910–1920
* Frank Oldfield of the United States Postal Inspection Service infiltrates the Black Hand Society and shuts down a branch of the Italian mafia in Central Ohio
1920–1930
* The Bureau of Prohibition launches many intelligence operations
1940–1950
* July 11, 1941 – Franklin D. Roosevelt appoints William J. Donovan as the Coordinator of Information, and establishes the Office of the Coordinator of Information
* June 13, 1942 – F.D.R. dissolves the Office of the Coordinator of Information, establishes the Office of Strategic Services (OSS)
* October 1, 1945 – President Truman signs Executive Order 9621 disbanding the OSS
* January 22, 1946 – President Truman directs the establishment of the Central Intelligence Group and the National Intelligence Authority
* January 22, 1946 – Sidney Souers is appointed the Director of the Central Intelligence Group
* September 18, 1947 – United States Congress passes the National Security Act of 1947, creating the Central Intelligence Agency and the United States Air Force
* June 20, 1949 – Congress passes the Central Intelligence Agency Act, allowing the CIA to establish slush funds and front companies in order to raise funds for covert and clandestine operations
1950–1960
* September 20, 1961 – First employees move in to the CIA Headquarters Building
1970–1980
* January 4, 1975 – President Ford signs Executive Order 11828, creating the Commission on CIA Activities within the United States
* January 27, 1975 – United States Senate establishes the Church Committee
* February 19, 1975 – United States House of Representatives establishes a temporary House Select Committee on Intelligence to investigate "illegal or improper" activities of federal intelligence agencies here or abroad
* February 19, 1976 – President Ford signs Executive Order 11905
* April 26, 1976 – Church Committee concludes investigations and submits final report
* May 19, 1976 – United States Senate establishes the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
* July 14, 1977 – House of Representatives establishes the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence
* August 4, 1977 – President Carter reorganizes the United States Intelligence Community, and creates a higher-level committee to be chaired by the Director of Central Intelligence
* January 24, 1978 – President Carter signs Executive Order 12036
1980–1990
* December 4, 1981 – President Reagan signs Executive Order 12333, reorganizing the Intelligence Community yet again
* June 23, 1982 – President Reagan signs the Intelligence Identities Protection Act
* October 15, 1984 – President Reagan signs the Central Intelligence Agency Information Act
2000–2010
* 2004 – Director of National Intelligence position is established, replacing the duties of the Director of Central Intelligence
* 2005 – Director of the Central Intelligence Agency position is established
2010–2020
